advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Dedupe restore_deleted_sources output across the primary and fallback passes in dry_run (e.g. update `have` in the dry_run primary branch or track already-appended names).
evidence: fsck_restore.py:154-156 primary dry_run branch: `if dry_run:` / `restored.append(name)` / `continue` — no file written, `have` not updated
fsck_restore.py:100 `for missing_uuid in snapshot_missing_sources(ticket_dir):` — under dry_run nothing was written so the same uuid is still reported
fsck_restore.py:106 `if name in have or name + RETIRED_SUFFIX in have:` — `have` was not updated by the dry_run primary loop, so this does not dedupe
fsck_repair.py:615 `if len(candidates) >= len(absent):` — a double-counted candidate can flip an unrecoverable ticket to 'would restore … then rebuild'
advisory.finding: In dry_run mode, restore_deleted_sources can return the same filename twice. The primary loop appends `name` without writing a file or adding to `have`; _uuid_fallback then re-derives the same missing uuid from snapshot_missing_sources (still reported missing because dry_run wrote nothing) and _deleted_path_for_uuid re-finds the same path — the `name in have` guard misses it since `have` was never updated. The duplicate inflates len(candidates) in _dry_run_plan.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the dry_run primary branch, also mark the name as seen (e.g. add `name`/`name+RETIRED_SUFFIX` to `have`) so _uuid_fallback's `name in have` guard filters it, matching the non-dry-run behavior.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the run_git show and file write in _uuid_fallback in the same OSError/SubprocessError guard the primary loop uses, logging-and-continuing on failure.
evidence: fsck_restore.py:111 `blob = run_git(tracker, "show", f"{commit}^:{path}", check=False, text=False)` — not wrapped in try/except
fsck_restore.py:114-115 `with open(os.path.join(ticket_dir, name + RETIRED_SUFFIX), "wb") as fh:` / `fh.write(blob.stdout)` — unguarded
fsck_restore.py:157-168 primary loop wraps the identical run_git show and open/write in `try/except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError)` and logs 'could not restore'
advisory.finding: _uuid_fallback drops the OSError/SubprocessError handling that the primary restore loop keeps: run_git show and the open()/write are unguarded, so an OSError (e.g. write failure, unreadable path) will propagate out of restore_deleted_sources instead of being logged and skipped like the primary path does.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 321 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 85fa-99e1-c81b-4fa2 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 85fa-99e1-c81b-4fa2` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 85fa-99e1-c81b-4fa2` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 85fa-99e1-c81b-4fa2 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
